definition: Techniques for adapting a model trained on data from one domain (the source) to perform well on a different but related domain (the target).
details: Domain adaptation is important when the distribution of deployment data differs from training data, such as adapting a model trained on formal text to perform well on informal social-media text.
story: Imagine teaching a friend to shoot a basketball. They miss, and you walk them backwards through the shot — elbow, wrist, release — to find what needs fixing. It is the same loop you use to learn anything: try, miss, correct, try again. Underneath all the magic is a patient process of small improvements. It is learning from every miss instead of repeating the same mistake. And that is Domain Adaptation — the quiet loop that turns flailing into skill.
